original_value: Recently, researchers have started exploring the design of route protection schemes that ensure networks can sustain traffic demand without congestion under failures. Existing approaches focus on ensuring worst-case performance over simultaneous f-failure scenarios is acceptable. Unfortunately, even a single bad scenario may render the schemes unable to protect against any f-failure scenario. In this paper, we present Lancet, a system designed to handle most failures when not all can be tackled. Lancet comprises three components: (i) an algorithm to analyze which failure scenarios the network can intrinsically handle which provides a benchmark for any protection routing scheme, and guides the design of new schemes; (ii) an approach to efficiently design a protection schemes for more general failure sets than all f-failure scenarios; and (iii) techniques to determine which of combinatorially many scenarios to design for. Our evaluations with real topologies and validations on an emulation testbed show that Lancet outperforms a worst-case approach by protecting against many more scenarios, and can even match the scenarios that can be handled by optimal network response.

result.paraphrase: Researchers have recently begun studying route protection schemes that keep networks able to carry traffic demand without congestion during failures. Current methods emphasize acceptable worst-case behavior across simultaneous f-failure cases. However, even one pathological case can make a scheme unable to protect against any f-failure scenario. In this paper, we introduce Lancet, a system built to cope with most failures when not all can be addressed. Lancet has three parts: (i) an algorithm that identifies which failure scenarios the network can inherently tolerate, providing a benchmark for any protection routing scheme and informing the design of new ones; (ii) a method for efficiently designing protection schemes for broader failure sets than all f-failure scenarios; and (iii) techniques for choosing which scenarios to design for among combinatorially many possibilities. Evaluations on real topologies and validations on an emulation testbed show that Lancet beats a worst-case approach by protecting against many more scenarios, and can even match the scenarios handled by optimal network response.
